query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) of refractory BCC high-entropy alloys (e.g., Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr based) induces a beneficial phase transformation and defect reconfiguration that improves ductility and uniform deformability without compromising high strength or impact-induced energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or as-deposited BCC refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr based) with inherent dislocation networks and phase stability characteristics.
generation.intervention: Application of deep cryogenic treatment (DCT), for example by immersing the alloy in a cryogenic medium (e.g., liquid nitrogen) for a specified duration post-fabrication.
generation.conditions: The treatment is applied after primary processing (e.g., laser melting deposition) under controlled cooling and hold times at cryogenic temperatures; the hypothesis holds under conditions where the alloy's BCC structure can undergo minor phase transformation and defect annealing without promoting detrimental embrittlement.
generation.structural_mediator: Induced phase transition and redistribution/annihilation of defects (e.g., dislocations), leading to a microstructure that supports multiple slip systems and enhanced plasticity.
generation.mechanism: DCT creates thermal stresses that promote a controlled phase transformation and refine the dislocation structure, thereby increasing the number of operative slip systems, which improves ductility and uniform deformability; simultaneously, the intrinsic high strength and impact-induced energy release characteristics are maintained because the phase change does not compromise the alloy’s load-bearing framework.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated baseline, DCT-treated alloys are expected to show significantly improved ductility (potentially on the order of 10–50% increase in elongation) and more uniform deformability, while tensile strength and impact-induced energy release remain at or near baseline values.
generation.baseline: As-cast or as-deposited refractory high-entropy alloys processed without deep cryogenic treatment that exhibit typical strength–ductility balances and energetic responses.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for refractory BCC high-entropy alloys where the cryogenic treatment prompts a favorable phase transition; the extent of benefit may be alloy-dependent and may not translate to systems with different crystal structures or compositions (e.g., alloys already optimized via chemical doping such as excessive cerium addition).
generation.uncertainty: While evidence from HfNbTaTiZr alloys in biomedical applications suggests DCT can enhance both strength and ductility, the scalability and precise balancing of energetics in high-entropy energetic structural materials remain moderately uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical refractory high-entropy alloy samples (e.g., Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr based) via laser melting deposition. Subject one set to deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) at liquid nitrogen temperature for a predetermined duration; retain the other set as the control. Perform static tensile tests and dynamic impact tests on both sets to measure mechanical properties and energy release behavior.
measurements: Tensile strength and elongation at break (ductility) from tensile testing
Uniformity of deformation observed through microstructural analysis (e.g., using electron microscopy)
Impact-induced energy release measured via ballistic or dynamic compression tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DCT-treated samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in ductility and uniform deformability (e.g., less than a 10% increase in elongation) while maintaining tensile strength and impact energy release within ±10% of the control group, the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser melting deposition, high entropy alloy, deep cryogenic treatment, 3D printing, defects, strength–ductility synergistic improvement

## Abstract
AbstractEnergetic structural materials play an important role in improving the damage performance of future weapons. To improve the energy-releasing behavior, Al0.5NbZrTi1.5Ta0.8Cex high-entropy alloys were prepared by vacuum-arc melting. The results showed the presence of BCC and FCC phases in the alloy with dendritic-morphology-element segregation and there were significant dislocations in the alloys. The current study focused on the effects of cerium content on the dynamic compressive mechanical and energetic characteristics. Cerium doping enhanced the energy-releasing characteristics of high-entropy alloys. The severity of the reaction increased with the increase in the cerium content, while the dynamic compressive strength generally decreased with the increase in cerium content. The Al0.5NbZrTi1.5Ta0.8Ce0.25 showed excellent mechanical and energy-releasing characteristics.
